summary: MSI driver catalog cache corruption stalls Intune enrollment on refurbished Windows devices
description: Issue summary: Several recently refurbished Windows notebooks are failing to complete corporate enrollment via Intune during out-of-box provisioning. Enrollment stalls at 'Applying device policies' and never progresses. Impact: Blocks provisioning of refurbished fleet (approx 12 devices seen so far), delaying deployments for a field engineering cohort and causing hardware to be returned to staging. Background: Devices are refurbished units that go through the depot imaging flow. Image applies successfully, but during first-boot Intune MDM enrollment stalls for an extended period. Observed behavior: - Devices reach Azure AD join and show as HybridJoined in local logs. - MDM client (DeviceManagementEnrollment) logs report repeated errors when fetching driver catalog metadata. - Windows driver catalog verifier returns erroneous signer hash mismatch for a cached catalog entry. Steps to reproduce: 1) Take a refurbished device from depot imaging pool. 2) Apply corporate staged image (build 2026.02.18). 3) Complete OOBE until network attach then allow AAD/Intune enrollment to run. 4) Observe UI stuck at 'Applying device policies' and Event Viewer Application/Operational logs for DeviceManagement-Enterprise-Diagnostics-Provider. Expected behavior: Enrollment completes and device receives configuration/policies within 10 minutes. Actual: Enrollment stalls indefinitely and MDM reports repeated driver catalog parse/hash failures, correlating with a corrupted local catalog cache (catdb). Sample event excerpts: "Enrollment failed with error 0x80070015" and "Driver signer hash mismatch: expected 3f1a..., found 0000...". Attachments: - Extracts from Event Viewer (supplied) - Intune enrollment trace (EMTelemetry) - Disk image of C:\Windows\System32\CatRoot2\catdb (uploaded to internal share).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:45 Priya Sharma: Initial ticket created after depot technician reported 6 devices in staging failing enrollment. Collected Event Viewer logs and uploaded to S3 share.

2026-03-10 11:20 Diego Ramos: Reproduced on Dell Latitude 7440 in lab. Confirmed repeated driver catalog parser failures. CatRoot2 timestamps indicate recent write anomalies during first boot. Marking as P1 due to blocked fleet.

2026-03-11 08:15 Evelyn Park (SRE): Checked image bake job logs. No errors during sysprep stage. Hypothesis: a race between depot firmware update agent (OEM TelemetryUpdater) and System Component Store writing catalog cache causing partial file writes.

2026-03-12 14:05 Markus Li (Imaging): Tested a modified imaging sequence that disables OEM telemetry service prior to sealing. Device enrollments completed normally (3/3). Need triage to confirm safe sequence change for depot process.
2026-03-13 10:30 Diego Ramos: Re-ran long-form repro with driverstore logger enabled. Found MD5 of cached cat file truncated at 0x1A400. Linked a sample binary to internal artifacts.
2026-03-13 16:50 Priya Sharma: Field staging paused on refurb batch #23. Logistics notified to hold shipments.
investigation_notes: Summary of investigation steps: - Reproduced failure on lab devices with same image and depot configuration. - Correlated catdb truncation to presence of OEM TelemetryUpdater service starting at first boot (service starts automatically and performs deferred firmware telemetry collection). - When OEM service runs concurrently with system Component Store writes (two processes flushing catalog metadata), the catdb file write sometimes becomes truncated/corrupted leading to signer hash mismatches during driver validation. - Disabling the OEM service before first boot eliminates the failure. - No evidence of filesystem-level hardware fault (SMART OK, no disk IO errors). - Intune server-side logs show enrollment handshake succeeded, but policy application aborted when local driver verification failed.
resolution: Workaround implemented: Depot imaging runbook updated to disable OEM TelemetryUpdater service prior to sealing images. For already-failed devices: manual remediation process created — boot into Windows PE, replace CatRoot2\catdb with known-good copy from image cache and allow enrollment to proceed. Status: temporary workaround deployed; full fix in progress.
workaround: 1) For new refurb batches: modify imaging pipeline to run 'sc config OEMTelemetryUpdater start= disabled' in offline image and confirm service disabled in audit step. 2) For affected devices in staging: boot WinPE, rename C:\Windows\System32\CatRoot2\catdb.corrupt -> catdb.bak and restore catdb.good from image cache, then reboot and re-trigger enrollment.
next_steps: - Engineering to add atomic write guarding around catalog updates in imaging scripts (imaging-scripts PR #88). - Contact OEM to request telemetry updater change to avoid starting during OOBE. - Validate change on 50-device pilot before closing. - Add automated check in depot QA to verify CatRoot2 integrity post-seal.
estimated_impact: ~12 devices observed, potential for larger impact if not fixed (full refurb fleet ~800 devices per month)
